[b]Launch of the THEP partnership program[/b]

THEP has today decided to take another step forwards towards global peace, democracy and cooperation through launching the [b]partnership program[/b].

This program will provide a way for non-THEP members to interact with the alliance and cooperate with the alliance, without having to adhere to the alliances full terms.

Membership to the program is open to all nations on Erene. You may submit an application to either [nation]United Hydronia[/nation] or [nation]the crystalline empire[/nation] on the RMB.

Additionally, upon the launch of this program, THEP would like to extend invitations to the following nations to take part in the program as its first ever members.

[nation]Lavinsworth United Islands[/nation]
[nation]Nordiheim[/nation]
[nation]Enkia[/nation]
[nation]Tallisland[/nation]
[nation]Akhratia[/nation]
[nation]Camphill[/nation]
[nation]Tan srpka[/nation]
[nation]Tarzania0[/nation] (my alt lmao)
[nation]Skullsbrough[/nation]
[nation]Karcovshkie[/nation]

You may accept or decline this invitation as you wish.

More info can be found here: https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2697019

[i][b]New Horizo- Homelands???[/b][/i]

After the still illigal occupation of Nestor Island by the Technokratisches Kaiserreich, the Sikirskian Government sent out the [nation]Sikirskian Colonial Administration[/nation] to search of new lands upon Sikirsk's home continent, West Shamat, and surrounding regions. Two results eventually arrived to Marshal-President John Mitarski's desk, the first was, so called, the North Pole.

[b]----------[/b]

The North Pole was known for being, you know, empty. Nearly no real colonizers were present in the region, and no international laws forbade its settlement. As early as 1966, Sikirsk had already established a small outpost on a fragment of its northern coast. Though often forgotten in history, this modest settlement endured, becoming a quiet but enduring symbol of Sikirskian persistence in hostile lands.

Now, decades later, the [nation]Sikirskian Colonial Administration[/nation] has returned with a bold proposal: to transform this isolated outpost into a true northern frontier. The plan envisions extending Sikirskian presence far deeper into the polar region, not merely as a matter of prestige, but as a demonstration of technological and logistical strength. The icy north, once dismissed as barren, is increasingly seen as a strategic prize, rich in untapped resources, and will be a somewhat great symbol of the Federation's goals.

Within the chamber of the Council of the Federation, debate has grown larger, to say the least. Supporters argue that a full-scale expansion will not only secure Sikirsks place as the rightful order of the north but also strengthen its energy independence and strategic depth. Opposition warns of overextension, costly infrastructure, and the ethical implications of disturbing fragile polar ecosystems. But eventually, the Marshal-President, chose for...: Yes.

[u][i][b]Gloria Federatska![/b][/i][/u]
